intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the labyrinthine streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes such as Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or self-guide using a map of the 36 guild streets.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on the night of the full moon when the town turns off electric lights and fills the streets and Thu Bon River with hundreds of colorful silk lanterns. Release a flower lantern on the river, browse artisan stalls, and soak in the magical cultural atmosphere.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, a dramatic mountain road stretching between Da Nang and Hue. Enjoy sweeping views of the South China Sea, jungle-covered peaks, and old French and American war fortifications at the summit. A quintessential backpacker experience in Central Vietnam.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, traveling by small wooden sampan through narrow canals lined with coconut palms and floating markets. Visit a coconut candy workshop, sample tropical fruits, and observe the daily riverside life of local communities in this fertile river delta region.

experiences.name: Banh Mi and Cao Lau Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join an affordable hands-on cooking class in Hoi An where a local chef teaches you to make signature Central Vietnamese dishes including Cao Lau noodles and freshly baked Banh Mi. Classes typically include a visit to the local market to source ingredients, giving deep insight into Vietnamese culinary culture and street food traditions.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the affordable 86 Express Bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check into Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk through the narrow streets of the 36 Ancient Streets district. Explore Hang Gai, Hang Bac, and Hang Dao streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the iconic view of Turtle Tower at dusk. Walk across the red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (entry ~30,000 VND). Afterward, dive into the buzzing Old Quarter Night Market on Hang Dao Street — browse souvenirs, street snacks, and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street cart near the airport or Old Quarter upon arrival (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local street stall on Hang Manh or Ly Quoc Su Street (~50,000–70,000 VND). Wash it down with a Bia Hoi (fresh draught beer, ~10,000 VND) at a corner plastic-stool spot.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or a reputable gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid taxi touts — use the 86 Express Bus or Grab app for affordable, safe transport. Keep small bills handy for street food.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a Vietnamese coffee (ca phe trung – egg coffee) at Cafe Giang on Nguyen Huu Huan Street (~30,000 VND) — a Hanoi institution. Then walk to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning tai chi spectacle with locals. Visit the ornate Ngoc Son Temple in full daylight if skipped last night. Stroll to St. Joseph's Cathedral, a stunning French Gothic church just minutes from the Old Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND, ~30 min by Grab) for a fascinating look at Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups with outdoor reconstructed stilt houses. Return to the Old Quarter and explore the Dong Xuan Market — Hanoi's largest covered market — for local goods, fabrics, and cheap snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the famous Hanoi Old Quarter Weekend Walking Street (pedestrian zone active on weekends; if a weekday, explore Bia Hoi Corner at the junction of Luong Ngoc Quyen and Ta Hien Streets). Watch street performers, mingle with locals, and soak in the chaotic energy.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) at Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street or a nearby Old Quarter pho stall (~50,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) at a stall near Dong Xuan Market (~45,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill) — try the affordable version at small restaurants on Cha Ca Street (~80,000–100,000 VND). Follow with Bia Hoi at Ta Hien Corner (~10,000–15,000 VND per glass).

day_by_day.notes: The Museum of Ethnology is closed on Mondays. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Hanoi's Old Quarter is best explored on foot. Beware of motorbike traffic when crossing streets — cross slowly and steadily.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free entry, open Tue–Thu & Sat–Sun mornings, ~8:00–11:00). See the Presidential Palace gardens, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house (~40,000 VND), and the One Pillar Pagoda (free). Dress respectfully — no shorts or sleeveless tops inside the mausoleum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, dating to 1070 (~30,000 VND). Spend 1–2 hours exploring the beautiful courtyards and stone steles. Afterward, visit Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') (~30,000 VND) for a sobering but essential historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND for budget seats) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Then wander back through the Old Quarter for a final evening street food crawl.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean) from a street vendor near the hotel (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls with pork and mushroom) at a local eatery near Ba Dinh Square (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl: Nem Ran (fried spring rolls, ~20,000 VND), Banh Mi (~25,000 VND), and fresh fruit from Old Quarter vendors. Total: ~60,000–80,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Book water puppet show tickets in advance or arrive 30 minutes early. The mausoleum is closed on Mondays, Fridays, and October–November for maintenance. Carry your passport or a copy for entry to some sites.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat Bus Station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~70,000–90,000 VND one way). Alternatively, book a budget day tour from the Old Quarter (~200,000–300,000 VND including transport). Upon arrival, rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000/day) and cycle to Trang An Grottoes — a UNESCO World Heritage landscape of karst mountains and river caves. Take a 2-hour boat tour through the grottoes (~200,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND entry) — Vietnam's 10th-century capital with ancient temples. Then climb the 500 steps up Mua Cave (Hang Mua) for a breathtaking panoramic view of the rice paddies and karst landscape (~100,000 VND entry). The view is one of the most spectacular in northern Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus in the late afternoon/early evening. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 19:00–20:00. Rest and enjoy a simple dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street cart before departure (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Nieu (clay pot rice) or fresh goat meat (de nui) — a Ninh Binh specialty — at a local restaurant near Hoa Lu (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Simple bowl of Bun Cha or pho at a local Old Quarter restaurant upon return (~50,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Start early (6:30–7:00 AM) to maximize time in Ninh Binh and avoid midday heat. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. The boat tour at Trang An is non-negotiable — don't skip it. Budget total for the day: ~500,000–600,000 VND (~$20–25 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hanoi accommodation. Take a Grab to Hanoi Railway Station or the airport. Board an early morning train or flight to Da Nang (~1 hour flight from ~500,000 VND on budget airlines like VietJet/Bamboo, or ~14-hour overnight train from ~300,000–500,000 VND for a soft sleeper). If flying, aim for a morning departure. From Da Nang, take a local bus or shared shuttle (~50,000–80,000 VND) to Hoi An Ancient Town (~45 min).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check into a budget guesthouse near the Ancient Town (~150,000–250,000 VND/night). Drop bags and take a slow walk through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town — admire the Japanese Covered Bridge, colourful lantern-draped streets, and French-colonial architecture. Entry ticket to the Ancient Town heritage sites is ~120,000 VND (covers 5 sites).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hoi An Night Market along the Thu Bon River. Browse handmade lanterns, silk goods, and local crafts. Watch the lanterns float on the river — especially magical near the Full Moon Festival (check dates). Enjoy the vibrant, laid-back atmosphere unique to Hoi An.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick Banh Mi or coffee near Hanoi hotel before checkout (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport/train snack or convenience store (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and herbs) at a street stall in the Ancient Town (~45,000–60,000 VND) — only authentic here due to local well water used in preparation.

day_by_day.notes: Book flights/trains in advance for best budget prices. VietJet and Bamboo Airways often have flash sales. If taking the overnight train from Hanoi, you save a night's accommodation cost. Hoi An is very walkable and bicycle-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from town) for a relaxed morning swim. The beaches are less crowded in the morning. Alternatively, explore the Ancient Town early when it's quiet — visit Tan Ky Ancient House (included in heritage ticket), the Fujian Assembly Hall, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget cooking class (~200,000–350,000 VND) — many guesthouses and local schools offer affordable half-day sessions where you visit the market, learn to make Banh Xeo (sizzling pancakes), White Rose Dumplings, and Cao Lau. This is a highlight of any Hoi An visit. Return to town and browse the tailors on Tran Phu Street if interested in custom clothing (budget ~300,000–500,000 VND for a simple item).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Thu Bon Riverside at sunset — one of the most picturesque scenes in Vietnam. Release a lantern on the river (~20,000–30,000 VND). Enjoy the festive lantern-lit streets of the Ancient Town after dark.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — the most famous Banh Mi in Vietnam (featured by Anthony Bourdain), on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~35,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Fried Wontons at a local eatery in the Ancient Town (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at a local restaurant on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~45,000–55,000 VND) — another Hoi An specialty not to miss.

day_by_day.notes: Avoid cycling during peak midday heat (11:00–14:00). Bargain politely at the market and tailor shops. The cooking class is one of the best value-for-money experiences in Vietnam — book directly with local schools to avoid commission markups.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (My Son Sanctuary & Hoi An Exploration)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning trip to My Son Sanctuary (~45 km from Hoi An), a UNESCO World Heritage Site of ancient Cham Hindu temples dating back to the 4th century. Join a budget group tour (~150,000–200,000 VND transport + ~150,000 VND entry) or rent a motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) and go independently. Arrive early (before 9:00) to beat the heat and tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An by early afternoon. Explore the less-visited areas: the Cam Nam island across the river (free, walk across the bridge) for a glimpse of authentic local village life away from tourist crowds. Visit a local pottery workshop or lantern-making workshop (~50,000–100,000 VND to participate).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Hoi An — treat yourself to a sunset drink at a rooftop bar with river views (one drink minimum, ~50,000–80,000 VND). Then enjoy a final street food dinner and pick up any last souvenirs — handmade lanterns make perfect lightweight gifts.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Man (savoury sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor (~25,000–35,000 VND) before departing for My Son
meals.lunch: Simple rice and vegetable dish (Com Binh Dan) at a local canteen near My Son or back in Hoi An (~35,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (Vietnamese sizzling pancake) at a local restaurant — wrap in rice paper with herbs and dip in fish sauce (~60,000–80,000 VND for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning — it gets extremely hot and crowded by 10:00 AM. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring water. If renting a motorbike, ensure you have an international driving permit and wear a helmet.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 - April 22, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hoi An guesthouse. Take a shuttle back to Da Nang Airport (~50,000–80,000 VND). Fly to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) on a budget airline (~400,000–700,000 VND, ~1.5 hours). Arrive in HCMC and take the 109 Airport Bus to Ben Thanh Market area (~20,000 VND) or a Grab to your budget hostel in District 1 or Bui Vien Street (~100,000–150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and drop bags. Head to Ben Thanh Market for a sensory overload of goods, spices, and street food. Walk to the nearby Reunification Palace (Dinh Thong Nhat, ~40,000 VND) — the historic building where the Vietnam War ended on April 30, 1975. Explore the preserved rooms and underground bunkers.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the famous Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's backpacker hub, alive with neon lights, street food, live music, and an electric atmosphere. Perfect for meeting fellow travellers. Explore the surrounding District 1 streets.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or airport snack before departure (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork, egg, and pickled vegetables) at a local stall near Ben Thanh (~45,000–60,000 VND) — the quintessential Saigon dish
meals.dinner: Street food on or near Bui Vien Street: Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls, ~30,000 VND), grilled skewers (~15,000–20,000 VND each), and a Tiger Beer (~25,000 VND). Total: ~80,000–100,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: HCMC traffic is intense — use Grab for longer distances and walk for short ones. Keep valuables close on Bui Vien Street and avoid displaying expensive cameras or phones. District 1 budget hostels range from ~100,000–200,000 VND/night in dormitories.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (HCMC History & Cu Chi Tunnels)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km from HCMC). Join a budget group tour (~150,000–250,000 VND including transport) or take a local bus (~20,000 VND) + local transport. The Cu Chi Tunnels are a remarkable 250 km network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong fighters during the war. Crawl through the tunnels, see booby traps, and gain a profound understanding of wartime Vietnam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) in District 3 — one of the most powerful and sobering war museums in the world. Then explore the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the historic Central Post Office (both free to view exteriors; post office interior is free).
day_by_day.evening: Explore District 4 for authentic local dining away from tourist markups. Walk along the Saigon River waterfront at night for city skyline views. End the evening at a rooftop bar in District 1 for a splurge drink with panoramic views (~80,000–120,000 VND for one cocktail).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (Banh Mi with fried egg) from a street cart (~25,000–35,000 VND) before departing for Cu Chi
meals.lunch: Simple Vietnamese lunch near Cu Chi Tunnels or packed snacks (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Cambodian-style clear noodle soup) in District 4 or 5 — a HCMC specialty (~50,000–70,000 VND). Followed by Che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup) from a street cart (~20,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum contains graphic imagery — be mentally prepared. Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Dinh site is closer and less commercialized than Ben Duoc. Wear old clothes to Cu Chi — crawling through tunnels is dusty. Book Cu Chi tours the night before through your hostel for best prices.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24, 2027 (Mekong Delta Day Trip & Departure Prep)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning budget day trip to the Mekong Delta (~1.5–2 hours from HCMC). Join a group tour to My Tho or Ben Tre (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport and boat ride). Cruise through narrow river channels on a traditional wooden sampan, visit a coconut candy workshop, sample tropical fruits (dragon fruit, jackfruit, rambutan), and hear traditional Southern Vietnamese folk music (Don Ca Tai Tu).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon (~14:00–15:00). Use the remaining time for last-minute souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the Russian Market (Cho Cu Ton That Dam) for better prices. Pack bags and prepare for departure. Head to Tan Son Nhat International Airport via Grab or the 109 bus.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Vietnam's north and south — from Hanoi's ancient streets and Ninh Binh's karst landscapes to Hoi An's lantern-lit charm and HCMC's electric energy.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local morning eatery near your hostel (~50,000–60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh tropical fruits and local snacks included in the Mekong Delta tour, or a simple Com Binh Dan (rice plate) (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Final Vietnamese meal at the airport or a quick Com Tam near the hostel before departure (~50,000–70,000 VND). Treat yourself to a final Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da, ~25,000–35,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Tan Son Nhat. The Mekong Delta tour is a wonderful final experience — book through your hostel to avoid overpriced tourist agencies. Keep some VND for airport purchases; exchange remaining currency before the airport for better rates. Estimated total 10-day budget: ~3,500,000–5,000,000 VND (~$140–200 USD) excluding flights between cities.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transit from airport to Old Quarter boutique hotel (~45 min by taxi or airport bus). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around Hoan Kiem Lake (5 min from most Old Quarter hotels). Visit Ngoc Son Temple on the lake island, cross the iconic red Huc Bridge. Stroll the surrounding streets to get a feel for the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday; if not a weekend, wander Ta Hien Beer Street instead). Enjoy the buzzing atmosphere of the Old Quarter at night, sample street snacks, and settle in.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) near the hotel upon arrival — ~35,000–50,000 VND at a local stall
meals.dinner: Banh Mi 25 or a nearby Bun Cha street stall on Hang Manh Street — grilled pork with noodles and herbs for ~60,000–80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag may be a factor. Exchange some cash at the airport or a local ATM. Grab a local SIM card at the airport for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (open mornings only, closed Mon/Fri). See the Presidential Palace exterior, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (30 min by taxi/Grab) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter. Watch the traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND). Afterward, walk to Ta Hien Street for a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass).

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) at Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street — a Hanoi institution, ~60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (the 'Obama Bun Cha' spot) near the museum area — ~80,000–100,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — iconic Hanoi turmeric fish dish — ~150,000–180,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and during certain national holidays. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees). Book Water Puppet Show tickets in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter on foot — each street historically named after its trade (Hang Bac for silver, Hang Gai for silk, etc.). Visit St. Joseph's Cathedral and the surrounding French Quarter streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture. Spend 1.5–2 hours wandering the five courtyards.
day_by_day.evening: Take a cyclo (rickshaw) ride through the Old Quarter at dusk for a classic Hanoi experience (~150,000–200,000 VND for 30–45 min). End the evening at a rooftop bar on Luong Van Can Street for city views.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a street stall near Hang Ga Street — ~40,000–55,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (Vietnamese set lunch) at a local canteen near Temple of Literature — rice, meat, and 2–3 sides for ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Xoi Yen on Nguyen Huu Huan Street — sticky rice dishes, a beloved local evening staple — ~50,000–70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate cyclo prices before boarding. The Old Quarter is best explored on foot — traffic can be chaotic but is part of the experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi for Ninh Binh by bus or train (~2 hours, ~100,000–150,000 VND). Check into a mid-range guesthouse. Rent a bicycle and cycle to Tam Coc — the 'Halong Bay on land' — for a scenic boat ride through limestone karsts and rice paddies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat trip through Tam Coc's three caves (~150,000 VND for 2 hours). Afterward, cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda, a cave pagoda carved into the cliffs — a peaceful and photogenic cultural stop.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ninh Binh town on bicycle. Visit the local market area for evening street food. Rest early for a big day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice) or banh mi from a street cart near the Hanoi hotel before departure — ~30,000–40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or Bun (noodle soup) at a riverside restaurant in Tam Coc — ~70,000–90,000 VND
meals.dinner: De Nui (mountain goat) — Ninh Binh's local specialty — at a restaurant in town — ~120,000–160,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ninh Binh bus/train the night before. Bicycles can be rented near Tam Coc for ~50,000–70,000 VND/day. Boat ride vendors may try to sell handicrafts mid-trip — politely decline if not interested.

day_by_day.morning: Early start: visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital — Vietnam's 10th-century capital with two ancient temples dedicated to the Dinh and Le dynasties. Hire a local guide for context (~100,000–150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek or motorbike to Mua Cave (Hang Mua) — climb 500 steps to the hilltop for a panoramic view over the rice fields and karst landscape. One of the most iconic viewpoints in northern Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by afternoon bus/train. Check back into Old Quarter hotel. Spend the evening packing and preparing for the overnight train to Hue.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Pho at the Ninh Binh guesthouse or a nearby stall — ~40,000–60,000 VND
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks bought at the Ninh Binh market before the Mua Cave hike
meals.dinner: Quick Old Quarter dinner — Bun Rieu (crab and tomato noodle soup) at a street stall near Hang Be Market — ~55,000–75,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book overnight train from Hanoi to Hue in advance (SE trains are recommended; soft sleeper berth ~500,000–700,000 VND). Train departs Hanoi in the late evening (~19:00–22:00 depending on train). Mua Cave entrance fee ~100,000 VND.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue by train in the morning (~13-hour journey). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in the city center. Head to the Imperial Citadel (Dai Noi) — the UNESCO-listed former seat of the Nguyen dynasty. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the moats, gates, and royal halls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or hire a xe om (motorbike taxi) to visit the Royal Tombs — Tomb of Tu Duc is the most scenic and atmospheric (~100,000 VND entrance). The tomb complex includes lakes, pavilions, and forested grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River embankment at sunset. Visit Dong Ba Market for local crafts and evening snacks. End the night with a dragon boat cruise on the Perfume River (optional, ~150,000–200,000 VND).

meals.breakfast: Train breakfast or snacks from the train vendor
meals.lunch: Banh Khoai (Hue crispy pancake) at a local eatery near the Citadel — ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Com Hen (baby clam rice) and Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) at Lac Thien or a similar family-run restaurant — ~80,000–110,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Hue's Bun Bo Hue is spicier than Hanoi's pho — a must-try local specialty. The Imperial Citadel entrance fee is ~200,000 VND. Comfortable shoes recommended for the tomb grounds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip over the Hai Van Pass to Da Nang by motorbike or bus (~2.5 hours). The pass offers stunning coastal views. Stop at the top for photos. Arrive in Da Nang and visit the Marble Mountains — five marble and limestone hills with caves, pagodas, and panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hoi An Ancient Town (30 min by bus or Grab from Da Nang). Check into a mid-range homestay or guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Old Town on foot — Japanese Covered Bridge, merchant houses, assembly halls.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the lantern-lit streets of Hoi An at night — the town is magical after dark. Take a lantern boat ride on the Thu Bon River (~50,000–80,000 VND). Browse the night market.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi at a Hue street stall before departure — Hue is also famous for its banh mi variations — ~30,000–45,000 VND
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside shack near Da Nang's My Khe Beach — grilled fish, shrimp, and squid — ~120,000–180,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at Thanh Cao Lau or a street stall in the Old Town — ~60,000–80,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book Hoi An accommodation in advance — it fills up quickly. Ancient Town entrance ticket (~120,000 VND) covers visits to 5 heritage sites. Motorbike rental for Hai Van Pass is adventurous but optional — bus is safer and cheaper.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hoi An's surrounding countryside by bicycle — cycle to the Tra Que Vegetable Village (~3 km from town) and join a 1-hour farming and cooking experience (~150,000–200,000 VND). Learn about traditional herb and vegetable cultivation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (5–7 km from town) for a few hours of relaxation. Rent a sun lounger (~50,000–80,000 VND) and enjoy the Central Vietnam coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An Old Town. Take a hands-on Vietnamese cooking class (many options available, ~400,000–600,000 VND including market visit and 3-course meal). A highlight of any Vietnam trip.

meals.breakfast: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) at White Rose Restaurant — a Hoi An specialty — ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's most famous banh mi shop — ~35,000–50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared in your own cooking class — included in the class fee

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — Morning Glory Cooking School and Red Bridge are highly rated. Bicycle rentals in Hoi An are ~50,000–70,000 VND/day. Sunscreen is essential at the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early flight or sleeper bus from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC). Flight is ~1 hour (~800,000–1,200,000 VND with budget airlines). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in District 1 (Bui Vien backpacker area or Ben Thanh area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum — one of the most powerful and sobering museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War. Spend 1.5–2 hours. Afterward, explore the historic Ben Thanh Market for souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker strip — for a lively evening atmosphere. Enjoy live music, street food, and the city's electric nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or Xoi from a Hoi An street cart before heading to Da Nang airport — ~30,000–45,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) near Ben Thanh Market — a HCMC staple — ~60,000–90,000 VND
meals.dinner: Pho Quynh on Bui Vien Street or a nearby street stall — pho and spring rolls — ~70,000–100,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang–HCMC flight in advance (VietJet, Bamboo Airways, or Vietnam Airlines). War Remnants Museum entrance ~40,000 VND. Ben Thanh Market is tourist-oriented — bargain firmly or shop at nearby local markets for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest of HCMC, ~1.5 hours by bus or organized tour). Explore the 250 km network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong forces — an extraordinary piece of living history. Crawl through sections of the tunnels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) — frozen in time since 1975, with original furnishings and underground command rooms. Then stroll past Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office (French colonial architecture).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — head to a rooftop bar in District 1 (Chill Skybar or EON Heli Bar) for panoramic city views and a celebratory cocktail (~150,000–250,000 VND per drink). Finish with a farewell street food feast.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (egg banh mi) from a cart near the guesthouse — ~35,000–50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Snacks and local food at Cu Chi Tunnels site or a roadside restaurant on the way back — ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Final Vietnamese feast — Lau (hot pot) at a local restaurant in District 1 — ~150,000–200,000 VND per person; a social and delicious send-off

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels tours depart early from District 1 (~7:30–8:00 AM). Book through a reputable operator (~250,000–350,000 VND including transport). The tunnels are narrow and dark — not recommended for claustrophobic travelers. Keep departure logistics in mind for the following day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi (approx. 45-minute drive in a chauffeured vehicle).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street) and Hang Bac (Silver Street) to soak in the artisan atmosphere. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake for a serene cultural introduction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake, followed by a curated street food walking tour of the Old Quarter led by a private guide — sampling Banh Mi, Bun Cha, and Cha Ca at the most celebrated local stalls.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or a premium café near the Old Quarter such as Cafe Pho Co (hidden rooftop café with lake views)
meals.dinner: Private street food tour dinner experience through Old Quarter lanes, curated by a local culinary guide — multiple tasting stops including Bun Cha Huong Lien and Banh Cuon stalls

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from the flight. April in Hanoi is warm (~28°C) with occasional light showers — pack a light rain layer.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex — including the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Book an early slot to avoid crowds. Follow with a visit to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology for a deep cultural immersion into Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070. Enjoy a private calligraphy demonstration inside the grounds. Afternoon tea at Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi's Le Club Bar — a colonial-era landmark experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (premium front-row seats). Dinner at a refined Vietnamese restaurant in the French Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — Vietnamese Pho, fresh baguette, tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Lunch at KOTO Restaurant near Temple of Literature — a social enterprise restaurant with exceptional Vietnamese cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane — a celebrated French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant in a restored colonial villa in the French Quarter

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays — confirm the day's schedule. Dress modestly for temple and mausoleum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day luxury cruise departure to Ha Long Bay — private or small-group premium overnight cruise. Morning: scenic drive (approx. 3.5 hours) from Hanoi to Ha Long Bay with a private vehicle and guide. Board the cruise ship around noon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through hidden lagoons and limestone caves (Sung Sot Cave / Surprise Cave). Swimming stop at an emerald-water bay. Onboard cooking demonstration of Vietnamese spring rolls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck. Multi-course seafood dinner prepared by the ship's chef using freshly caught local seafood. Squid fishing activity off the deck under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch onboard the luxury cruise — fresh seafood, Vietnamese salads, and local delicacies
meals.dinner: Gourmet multi-course dinner onboard featuring Ha Long Bay seafood — lobster, grilled squid, steamed clams with lemongrass

day_by_day.notes: Book a premium cruise line such as Indochine Cruise, Perla Dawn Sails, or Paradise Elegance for the finest experience. Pack sunscreen, swimwear, and a light jacket for evenings on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the cruise deck at sunrise over Ha Long Bay. Explore a floating fishing village by rowboat with a local guide. Visit a pearl farm to learn about Ha Long's pearl cultivation tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return cruise to Ha Long pier. Private transfer back to Hanoi (or option to fly directly to Hue/Da Nang). Check into hotel and rest. Late afternoon: explore Hue's Imperial Citadel if travel day allows.
day_by_day.evening: If staying in Hanoi: evening at leisure in the Old Quarter — browse night market on Hang Dao Street, enjoy a Bia Hoi (fresh beer) experience at a premium corner spot. If traveled to Hue: gentle evening stroll along the Perfume River.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous brunch onboard before disembarkation — Dim Sum, tropical fruits, Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a seafood restaurant near Ha Long pier before transfer, or en route at a curated rest stop
meals.dinner: In Hanoi: Dinner at Cha Ca La Vong — the legendary turmeric fish restaurant operating since 1871. In Hue: Dinner at La Residence Hotel's Le Parfum restaurant overlooking the Perfume River

day_by_day.notes: Confirm onward travel logistics the evening before. If flying Hanoi to Hue, book Vietnam Airlines or Bamboo Airways business class for a premium domestic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Hue — the former Imperial Capital. Private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Imperial Citadel and Forbidden Purple City. Explore the ornate Thien Mu Pagoda by private dragon boat along the Perfume River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the elaborate Royal Tombs — Tomb of Minh Mang and Tomb of Tu Duc, set in serene forested landscapes. Private cyclo (rickshaw) ride through Hue's leafy boulevards. Visit a traditional Hue conical hat (Non La) workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Royal Hue cuisine dinner experience — a ceremonially presented multi-course meal replicating dishes once served to Vietnamese emperors, at a heritage restaurant or private villa setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel — Hue-style Banh Mi and Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup, a Hue specialty)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lac Thien or Lac Thanh — legendary family-run restaurants famous for authentic Hue cuisine, including Banh Khoai (crispy pancakes)
meals.dinner: Royal Dinner at Tinh Gia Vien — a restored aristocratic garden house serving imperial Hue cuisine in a candlelit courtyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Hue is best explored with a private guide to fully appreciate the historical depth. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Imperial Citadel covers a large area.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic Hai Van Pass drive (or train ride on the Reunification Express — book a premium cabin) from Hue to Da Nang. The Hai Van Pass offers some of Vietnam's most breathtaking coastal panoramas. Stop at the summit for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Da Nang. Visit the Marble Mountains — a cluster of five limestone hills with caves, pagodas, and panoramic views of the coastline. Explore the Dragon Bridge and Da Nang's modern waterfront. Check into a luxury beachfront resort on My Khe Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Stroll across the iconic Dragon Bridge (which breathes fire on weekend evenings). Dinner at a premium Da Nang seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hue hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Marble Mountains — Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) is a Da Nang specialty
meals.dinner: Dinner at Waterfront Restaurant Da Nang — an upscale riverside venue with panoramic city views and an extensive Vietnamese and international menu

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass road journey takes approx. 1.5 hours by car. The Reunification Express train from Hue to Da Nang takes about 2.5 hours — both offer spectacular scenery. Book train tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hoi An Ancient Town (30 km from Da Nang). Private guided walking tour of the UNESCO World Heritage Old Town — Japanese Covered Bridge, Assembly Halls, merchant houses, and silk lantern workshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bespoke tailoring experience — Hoi An is world-famous for custom clothing made within 24 hours. Visit a premium tailor (Yaly Couture or A Dong Silk) for a fitting. Explore the vibrant Hoi An Central Market and riverside promenade. Optional: cooking class at a premium culinary school (Red Bridge or Morning Glory).
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An by lantern light — the town transforms magically at dusk. Boat ride on the Thu Bon River releasing paper lanterns. Dinner at a top Hoi An restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Da Nang resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Morning Glory Restaurant — run by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy, renowned for authentic Hoi An cuisine including Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Deck House Hoi An — a beautifully restored riverside restaurant with refined Vietnamese cuisine and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Old Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Some areas restrict motorbikes. Pick up tailored clothing the following morning if ordering today. Evening lantern release is magical — bring cash for lanterns.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the Da Nang beach resort — spa treatment, swimming, or yoga on the beach. Optional: return to Hoi An to collect tailored clothing. Visit the Ba Na Hills by cable car (one of the world's longest) — explore the French Village and the famous Golden Bridge held by giant stone hands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ba Na Hills continued — explore Fantasy Park, the French-style gardens, and panoramic mountain views. Return to Da Nang by late afternoon. Fly or transfer to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — book business class domestic flight.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City. Check into a luxury hotel in District 1 (Park Hyatt Saigon or Caravelle Saigon recommended). Evening rooftop drinks at Saigon Saigon Bar (Caravelle) — a historic haunt of war correspondents with sweeping city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Da Nang resort — full Vietnamese and international spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ba Na Hills — restaurant within the French Village complex
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Saigon at Noir — Dining in the Dark, a unique sensory fine dining experience in Ho Chi Minh City

day_by_day.notes: Ba Na Hills can be crowded on weekends — visit early. The flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes. Confirm hotel check-in timing.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the War Remnants Museum and Reunification Palace — deeply moving and historically essential experiences that provide profound context for modern Vietnam. Visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the French colonial Central Post Office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ben Thanh Market with a private guide — navigate the organized chaos, sample local snacks, and shop for premium Vietnamese lacquerware, silk, and coffee. Visit the vibrant street art district of Bui Vien Street area. Afternoon coffee at The Workshop — Saigon's most celebrated specialty coffee roastery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Chill Skybar on the 26th floor — one of Saigon's most spectacular rooftop venues. Premium street food experience in District 1 — Banh Mi, Hu Tieu noodle soup, and Vietnamese iced coffee at celebrated local spots.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the luxury hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Propaganda Bistro — a stylish restaurant near the Reunification Palace serving elevated Vietnamese street food in a vibrant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuc Gach Quan — a beloved restored villa restaurant serving rustic, deeply authentic Vietnamese home cooking in an atmospheric garden setting

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allow time to process. Ben Thanh Market is best visited with a guide to avoid tourist pricing. Keep small cash denominations for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day private tour to the Cu Chi Tunnels — the extraordinary underground network used by Viet Cong guerrillas. Opt for the premium 'VIP tunnel' experience with exclusive access to wider sections. Return to Saigon by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon of leisure — visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu), one of Saigon's most atmospheric temples. Explore the upscale Dong Khoi Street for premium Vietnamese souvenirs — Saigon Kitsch, premium Trung Nguyen coffee sets, and silk goods. Optional: indulge in a final luxury spa treatment at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a world-class Saigon restaurant. Final stroll along the Saigon Riverfront promenade. Transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure (if applicable) or extend stay.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — enjoy a final Vietnamese Pho and Banh Mi spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Cu Chi or back in District 1 — Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle bowl) is a must-try
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at The Restaurant at Park Hyatt Saigon — sophisticated Vietnamese and international cuisine in an elegant colonial setting, with a curated cocktail and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels tour departs early — confirm pickup time with your guide. Pack any purchased items securely for the return journey. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in. Consider purchasing premium Vietnamese coffee, silk, and lacquerware as final gifts.
